structural-causal.name: bottleneckControl
structural-causal.basis: Identity authorization is a control-plane bottleneck as human, service and AI-agent identities proliferate.

structural-causal.name: scenarioRobustness
structural-causal.basis: The need persists across cloud, hybrid and agentic adoption scenarios even if specific AI architectures change.

structural-causal.name: substitutionResilience
structural-causal.basis: Deep identity integrations and governance workflows create switching friction, but cloud suites and specialist identity vendors remain substitutes.

discovery-weak-signals.name: agentic identity demand

discovery-weak-signals.name: AI product conversion

adversarial-red-team.name: source dependence
adversarial-red-team.basis: The newest AI new-ARR mix and quarter details rely materially on independent press reporting rather than a same-period primary release in the packet.

adversarial-red-team.name: competitive response
adversarial-red-team.basis: Cloud/security suites can bundle identity governance and compress standalone differentiation.

adversarial-red-team.name: confidence inflation
adversarial-red-team.basis: Strong ARR does not by itself prove durable pricing power or AI-specific unit economics.

expectations-execution.name: ARR execution
expectations-execution.basis: ARR growth and raised guidance indicate recurring-demand resilience.

expectations-execution.name: expectation sensitivity
expectations-execution.basis: A modest revenue miss accompanied otherwise strong recurring metrics and muted share reaction.
